doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Becoming a US citizen in January 2020
summary: She became a citizen after 26 years, describing the Bridgeport ceremony, a two-hour passport, and hopes for the country.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Do you think it’s hard for you because — I lost track if you’re a citizen or not.
I became a citizen in January.

After 26 years here. So I definitely feel like I’m part of the fabric of the country, you know what I mean? I mean I paid my taxes the first year and I’ve always been legal, and I’ve always wanted to do things the right way here you know. And I always — it was a beautiful ceremony in January. A very different time. Not so long ago, but a really different feeling in January. And there were, how many of us, I forgot the number of us
now, 55 or something at a court in Bridgeport. Was it Bridgeport? I think it was Bridgeport.

And it was federal court and we all turned out, all dressed up. And it was a very moving speech that the judge gave and handed out certificates. And the next day I went down to the Passport Expedite Service in Stamford, and I got a passport in two hours. I could not believe it. I mean it was like, okay, that I’m impressed with. That impressed me because I said I’m going on a jazz cruise next week and I just became a U.S. citizen and I need a passport. And I said, “By the way I have to fly to North Carolina tonight for a jazz festival and I’ll be back on Monday.” And they said, “Give me a minute.” And they went away and they came back and said, “Can you come back at 12:00 today?” I said, “Yes, my flight is not until 6. Absolutely.” So I went away and had a cup of coffee, came back and got a passport. I couldn’t believe it. I just became a citizen and the next day I had a passport. I thought well this is too good to be true. So some things do work when they’re supposed to work and that was impressive you know? And I’m really glad because everything’s been shut down since then and my case was already delayed way longer than it should have been because of the amount that I travel. So I had to get my local senator to contact Immigration and it was a process and a half to get there. So by the time we got to our ceremony it was oh, thank goodness, you know? It’s done, I’m a citizen and I’m a dual citizen and I’m really proud to be a dual citizen. I want to vote. I want to participate. I want all the things that every citizen of a country wants, you know? Yes I think that things could have been handled way better and I really hope that things don’t escalate in this country and get out of control, and that the good people shine through. The majority of people in this country are very good. And I believe that and I will still believe in that.
